description.value: The study assessed the effects of a single session of moderate-intensity exercise on regional brain activation in response to smoking-related and neutral images during temporary nicotine abstinence in smokers.

spans.text: The objective of the study was to assess the effect of exercise on regional brain activation in response to smoking-related images during temporary nicotine abstinence.

description.value: In a randomised crossover design, overnight abstinent smokers underwent an exercise and passive control treatment, with fMRI scanning after each treatment.

spans.text: In a randomised crossover design, overnight abstinent smokers ( n = 20) underwent an exercise (10-min moderate-intensity stationary cycling) and passive control (seating for the same duration) treatment, following 15 h of nicotine abstinence.

value: Comparisons between smoking and neutral images revealed significant activation in the insula and superior parietal lobe. Regardless of session type, smoking-related images elicited a significant cue response in areas including the superior parietal lobe and insula, regions associated with limbic processing and visual attention.

spans.text: Comparisons between smoking and neutral images from the random effects ANOVA revealed areas of activation including the insula and the superior parietal lobe (see Table 1 ; Fig. 3 ).

value: Following the control condition, regional brain activation was seen in the cuneus and middle and inferior occipital lobe in response to smoking images versus neutral images. These findings suggest heightened visual attention towards smoking-related stimuli during nicotine deprivation.

value: Following the exercise treatment, no areas of activation were seen for smoking images versus neutral images. A session of exercise may therefore downregulate activation in areas associated with attention and visual processing.

Having created a series of t-contrast images for each subject and each event, a random-effects (second level) analysis was carried out to assess (a) which voxels showed activation to smoking images compared to control images across the two treatments and (b) which voxels showed activation to smoking compared to neutral for each treatment.
Data were analysed using SPM5 Software ( www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm ).
An uncorrected statistical threshold p < 0.001 and a voxel cluster threshold of 10 were used.
